subQuestions.questionText:
A recent Covid-19 requirement for international travel:
A Visa application
B Proof of vaccination
C Cholera certificate
D International driver's licence
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
Proof of vaccination became a recent Covid-19 requirement for international travel.

subQuestions.questionText:
Ms Jones purchased jewellery to the value of R50 000 on a recent overseas trip. On arrival at South African customs, this purchase would fall under ...
A items to be declared.
B items not to be declared.
C duty-free allowances.
D prohibited items.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (1 mark)
Jewellery valued at R50 000 exceeds the duty-free allowance and must be declared as items to be declared.

subQuestions.questionText:
Sydney (+10) is ... hours ahead of Johannesburg (+2).
A 0
B 9
C 8
D 6
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (1 mark)
Sydney (+10) minus Johannesburg (+2) = 8 hours ahead.

subQuestions.questionText:
Jet fatigue is a travel-related condition caused by travelling ...
A across many time zones.
B on a long-haul flight.
C at odd times of the day.
D only at night.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
Jet fatigue is caused by travelling on a long-haul flight (as opposed to jet lag, which is caused by crossing time zones).

options.C: at odd times of the day.

subQuestions.questionText:
The bank selling rate is always ... the bank buying rate.
A lower than
B higher than
C equal to
D double
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
The bank selling rate is always higher than the bank buying rate, which is how the bank makes a profit.

subQuestions.questionText:
The famous wall in Israel used for prayers and confessions:
A Berlin Wall
B Southern Wall
C Wailing Wall
D Eastern Wall
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (1 mark)
The Wailing Wall (Western Wall) in Jerusalem, Israel, is used for prayers and confessions.

subQuestions.questionText:
Petra is located in this Middle Eastern country:
A Israel
B Jordan
C Lebanon
D Turkey
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
Petra, the ancient rock-cut city, is located in Jordan.

subQuestions.questionText:
The Swiss Alps are known as ...
A a sacred mountain range for locals.
B a range of mountains in Nepal.
C a mountain range popular for skiing holidays.
D the highest mountain range in the world.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (1 mark)
The Swiss Alps are a mountain range popular for skiing holidays.

options.A: a sacred mountain range for locals.
options.B: a range of mountains in Nepal.
options.C: a mountain range popular for skiing holidays.
options.D: the highest mountain range in the world.

subQuestions.questionText:
The Vredefort Dome and iSimangaliso Wetland Park have the following in common:
A Both are located in KwaZulu-Natal.
B Both are natural sites.
C Both are cultural sites.
D Both are located in North West.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
Both the Vredefort Dome and iSimangaliso Wetland Park are natural World Heritage Sites.

options.D: Both are located in North West.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the current brand image of South Africa. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (1 mark)
The current brand image of South Africa is 'South Africa - Inspiring new ways'.

subQuestions.questionText:
Guidelines regulating uniforms and other clothing to be worn during working hours:
A Dress code
B Media policy
C Packing policy
D Currency code
subQuestions.memoText:

A dress code provides guidelines regulating uniforms and clothing to be worn during working hours.

subQuestions.questionText:
A basic condition of employment included in a contract of employment:
A Financial challenges
B Product packaging
C Names of businesses
D Core duties
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (1 mark)
Core duties are a basic condition of employment included in a contract of employment.

subQuestions.questionText:
Many responsible tourism businesses adopt a pledge that will ...
A maximise the negative effects of crime.
B decrease the benefits from tourist visits.

D minimise the impact on the environment.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (1 mark)
Responsible tourism businesses adopt a pledge that will minimise the impact on the environment.

options.A: maximise the negative effects of crime.
options.B: decrease the benefits from tourist visits.
options.C: increase poaching in a protected area.
options.D: minimise the impact on the environment.

subQuestions.questionText:
Airline staff receive flight tickets at a discounted rate as a/an ...
A travel benefit.
B urban legend.
C mystery client.
D customs requirement.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (1 mark)
Discounted flight tickets for airline staff are a travel benefit.

subQuestions.questionText:
A sustainable practice when a lodge is built in an environmentally sensitive area:
A Trees are chopped down to build the lodge.
B Bricks are imported from a foreign country.
C Large areas are cleared to build the lodge.
D Wooden walkways are built around existing trees.
subQuestions.memoText:

Building wooden walkways around existing trees is a sustainable practice that protects the environment.

options.A: Trees are chopped down to build the lodge.
options.B: Bricks are imported from a foreign country.
options.C: Large areas are cleared to build the lodge.
options.D: Wooden walkways are built around existing trees.

subQuestions.questionText:
The G20 (Group of Twenty) gathering that took place in Bali, Indonesia, in November 2022, is an example of a/an ...
A global summit.
B local occurrence.
C political situation.
D unforeseen occurrence.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (1 mark)
The G20 gathering of heads of state is an example of a global summit.

subQuestions.questionText:
... is not a safe payment option when travelling internationally.
A A Diners Club debit card

Carrying large amounts of cash is not a safe payment option when travelling internationally.

options.D: A pre-loaded foreign exchange debit card

subQuestions.questionText:
An example of a political situation that can impact on tourism:

D Civil wars

A religious

A political situation.
B natural disaster.

D terror attack.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description by choosing a word/term from the list: physical appearance of the business; signage; promotes integrity; social gathering of the workers; company stationery; uniform allowances; grooming.

Branded paper and pens that improve the image of the hotel.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: company stationery (1 mark)
Branded paper and pens are examples of company stationery that improve the hotel's image.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description by choosing a word/term from the list: physical appearance of the business; signage; promotes integrity; social gathering of the workers; company stationery; uniform allowances; grooming.

Cleanliness of the travel agency and the surrounding gardens.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: physical appearance of the business (1 mark)
Cleanliness of the agency and gardens refers to the physical appearance of the business.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description by choosing a word/term from the list: physical appearance of the business; signage; promotes integrity; social gathering of the workers; company stationery; uniform allowances; grooming.

Acceptable haircut and short nails for male employees.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: grooming (1 mark)
An acceptable haircut and short nails are aspects of grooming.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description by choosing a word/term from the list: physical appearance of the business; signage; promotes integrity; social gathering of the workers; company stationery; uniform allowances; grooming.

The value of a code of conduct for tourist guides.
subQuestions.memoText:

A code of conduct promotes integrity among tourist guides.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description by choosing a word/term from the list: physical appearance of the business; signage; promotes integrity; social gathering of the workers; company stationery; uniform allowances; grooming.

Airlines contributing to the cost of the cabin crew's work wear.
subQuestions.memoText:

Airlines contributing to the cost of cabin crew work wear is an example of uniform allowances.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose the correct word(s) from those given in brackets.

An example of recycling is (re-visiting/re-using) plastic crates in which vegetables are delivered to a restaurant.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: re-using (1 mark)
Re-using plastic crates is an example of recycling.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose the correct word(s) from those given in brackets.

Using energy efficient light bulbs in a museum is an example of sustainable (management of resources/preservation of artifacts).
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: management of resources (1 mark)
Energy efficient light bulbs are an example of the sustainable management of resources.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose the correct word(s) from those given in brackets.

The removal of (alien plants/indigenous animals) is beneficial to the natural environment.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: alien plants (1 mark)
The removal of alien plants is beneficial to the natural environment.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose the correct word(s) from those given in brackets.

A tourism business making use of (grey water/sea water) for gardening purposes will attract environmentally conscious tourists.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: grey water (1 mark)
Using grey water for gardening attracts environmentally conscious tourists.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose the correct word(s) from those given in brackets.

A responsible tourist will pay a fair price for (mass-produced/handmade) souvenirs.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: handmade (1 mark)
A responsible tourist pays a fair price for handmade souvenirs to support local crafters.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a destination from COLUMN B that matches a global natural disaster in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: Many tourists had to cancel their holidays to this South African coastal province due to severe flooding in 2022.
COLUMN B options: A Philippines; B Madagascar; C Ecuador; D KwaZulu-Natal; E Texas; F Eswatini
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: D (KwaZulu-Natal) (1 mark)
Severe flooding in 2022 caused tourists to cancel holidays to the South African coastal province of KwaZulu-Natal.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a destination from COLUMN B that matches a global natural disaster in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: The January 2021 landslides caused major damage and disruptions in this Southern African neighbouring country.
COLUMN B options: A Philippines; B Madagascar; C Ecuador; D KwaZulu-Natal; E Texas; F Eswatini
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: F (Eswatini) (1 mark)
The January 2021 landslides caused major damage in the Southern African neighbouring country of Eswatini.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a destination from COLUMN B that matches a global natural disaster in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: Tropical storm Megi caused severe damage in this Southeast Asian country in April 2022.
COLUMN B options: A Philippines; B Madagascar; C Ecuador; D KwaZulu-Natal; E Texas; F Eswatini
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: A (Philippines) (1 mark)
Tropical storm Megi caused severe damage in the Southeast Asian country of the Philippines in April 2022.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a destination from COLUMN B that matches a global natural disaster in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: In February 2022, Cyclone Emnati caused devastation in this Indian Ocean island.
COLUMN B options: A Philippines; B Madagascar; C Ecuador; D KwaZulu-Natal; E Texas; F Eswatini
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: B (Madagascar) (1 mark)
Cyclone Emnati caused devastation on the Indian Ocean island of Madagascar in February 2022.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a destination from COLUMN B that matches a global natural disaster in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: Flights were delayed due to ash eruptions from Wolf Volcano in this South American country.
COLUMN B options: A Philippines; B Madagascar; C Ecuador; D KwaZulu-Natal; E Texas; F Eswatini
subQuestions.memoText:

Ash eruptions from Wolf Volcano delayed flights in the South American country of Ecuador.

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the World Heritage Site described below. Write only the name of the World Heritage Site.

World Heritage Site A is associated with the golden rhinoceros. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:

Mapungubwe, associated with the famous golden rhinoceros artefact, is World Heritage Site A.

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the World Heritage Site described below. Write only the name of the World Heritage Site.

World Heritage Site B exposes tourists to ancient mountainous landscapes in Mpumalanga. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)

The Barberton Makhonjwa Mountains in Mpumalanga expose tourists to ancient mountainous landscapes.

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the World Heritage Site described below. Write only the name of the World Heritage Site.

World Heritage Site C is South Africa's only mixed World Heritage Site. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Maloti-Drakensberg Park / uKhahlamba-Drakensberg Park (1 mark)
The Maloti-Drakensberg Park (uKhahlamba-Drakensberg Park) is South Africa's only mixed World Heritage Site.

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the World Heritage Site described below. Write only the name of the World Heritage Site.

World Heritage Site D displays evidence of the origins of mankind. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)

The Cradle of Humankind displays evidence of the origins of mankind.

subQuestions.questionText:

A former South African president was imprisoned at World Heritage Site E. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:

Former President Nelson Mandela was imprisoned at Robben Island, World Heritage Site E.

subQuestions.questionText: Read the information about philan-tourism and Mr Murdock (a philanthropist from Canada who travels to destinations in need of tourism development). Name ONE way, in the extract, how Mr Murdock is involved in philan-tourism.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE way:
• He spends time in a flood-affected area to assist the community in rebuilding the tourism infrastructure.
• He wants to make a positive social impact by spending time assisting the local community.
• He has chosen a destination in need of money that is generated by tourism.
• He is giving back to the community and contributing to the local economy.

subQuestions.questionText: Tourists from Canada do not require a visa when travelling to South Africa. Name the compulsory travel document Mr Murdock would require to enter South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• Passport

subQuestions.questionText: Mr Murdock may be required to present proof of a Covid-19 vaccination. Name the global organisation responsible for regulating the Covid-19 vaccinations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• World Health Organisation
• WHO

subQuestions.questionText: Recommend ONE health precaution to Mr Murdock when he visits the flood-affected area.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE precaution:
• Drink bottled water.
• Wear a mask.
• Sanitise regularly.
• Advisable to have taken the Covid-19 vaccine.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the term connecting flight.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• A flight that requires a passenger to change aeroplanes and take another flight to get to his final destination.
• A flight with a stop and a change of aircraft to get to the final destination.

subQuestions.questionText: Study the World Time Zone map and itinerary. Mr Murdock's flight departed from Vancouver International Airport at 18:00 on Saturday and the nonstop flight lasted 9 hours. Calculate the time and day in Frankfurt when Mr Murdock departed from Vancouver International Airport. Show ALL calculations. (Vancouver -8, Frankfurt +1) (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark allocation (4 marks):
Vancouver -8, Frankfurt +1
Time difference = 9 hours
18:00 (+) 9 hours
Time in Frankfurt = 03:00 on Sunday

Answer: 03:00 on Sunday

subQuestions.questionText: Mr Murdock arrived at Frankfurt International Airport at 12:00 on Sunday. His flight departed for South Africa at 16:00 on Sunday. Calculate how long he had to be in transit before his flight departed for South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark allocation (2 marks):
Arrival at Frankfurt = 12:00
Departure to South Africa = 16:00
Time in transit = 4 hours

Answer: 4 hours

subQuestions.questionText: Mr Murdock's flight departed Frankfurt for South Africa at 16:00 on Sunday and the flight lasted 11 hours. Calculate the time and day that Mr Murdock arrived in Johannesburg. Show ALL calculations. (Frankfurt +1, Johannesburg +2) (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark allocation (5 marks):
Frankfurt +1, Johannesburg +2
Time difference = 1 hour
16:00 (+) 1 hour = 17:00
17:00 (+) 11 hours (flying time)
Arrival in Johannesburg = 04:00 on Monday / next day

Answer: 04:00 on Monday

subQuestions.questionText: On arrival at OR Tambo International Airport, Mr Murdock proceeded to passport control, collected his luggage and went through customs. Choose the customs channel Mr Murdock had to proceed through on arrival at OR Tambo International Airport.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• Green channel

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason for your answer to QUESTION 2.3.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE reason:
• He has nothing to declare.
• The goods Mr Murdock brought into the country are within the duty-free limits.

subQuestions.questionText: Mr Murdock flew from OR Tambo International Airport to King Shaka International Airport and needed transport from the airport to the B&B, where there are many transport providers operating. Advise Mr Murdock on TWO safety considerations before selecting a transport provider.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each consideration (max 4 marks):
• He should use registered transport providers.
• He should get information from the information desk at the airport about registered, reputable (trustworthy) transport providers.
• He should never ask for help from a stranger about transport.
• Should he make use of the B&B's transport, he must ensure beforehand the name of the shuttle company and the contact details of the driver.

subQuestions.questionText: Mrs Murray, a tennis enthusiast, flew from South Africa to London to watch Wimbledon and spent four days in London. Give the name of the currency Mrs Murray needed for her trip to London.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• Great British Pound
• Pound Sterling
• British Pound

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the total cost in South African rand of Mrs Murray's trip to Wimbledon. (Non-stop return flight to London: R13 000; Visa costs: R2 950; Travel Insurance: R1 456; Wimbledon package: R37 850)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark allocation (2 marks):
R13 000 + R2 950 + R1 456 + R37 850
= R55 256

Answer: R55 256

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the amount in QUESTION 3.1.2 and to her total budget of R75 000. Calculate the amount in rand she had available to spend in London.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark allocation (2 marks):
R75 000 - R55 256
= R19 744

Answer: R19 744

subQuestions.questionText: Mrs Murray had sufficient spending money while visiting London. Do you agree with the statement above? Give TWO reasons for your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each reason (max 4 marks). NOTE: No marks are awarded for YES or NO.

YES / I agree:
• All her major expenses were paid and there was enough money left for spending to buy souvenirs and go on short trips.
• The duration of her stay in London was only for a period of four days.

OR

NO / I disagree:
• London is a very expensive city.
• This amount is far too little to spend in London once the rand has been converted into British pound.

subQuestions.questionText: Convert the total cost of the tour in QUESTION 3.1.2 (R55 256) to the currency used in London. (GBP Bank Selling Rate = 20,42) Round off your answer to TWO decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark allocation (3 marks):
R55 256 ÷ 20.42
= GBP2 705.97

Answer: GBP2 705.97

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the term fluctuation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• Fluctuation refers to the daily change of the value of one currency against other currencies.
• Fluctuation refers to the rising and falling of the value of currencies over a certain period.

subQuestions.questionText: The impact of the war between Russia and Ukraine, the ongoing Covid-19 pandemic and the floods in KwaZulu-Natal have had a negative impact on the value of the South African rand. Discuss in a paragraph the impact of a weak rand on the tourism industry in South Africa. Focus on ONE impact of the weak rand on inbound tourism (2) and TWO impacts on the multiplier effect in South Africa (4).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark allocation (6 marks):

ONE impact on inbound tourism (2 marks):
• Greater influx of inbound international tourists as South Africa will be seen as a value-for-money destination.
• Tourists will find South Africa an affordable destination to visit.

TWO impacts on the multiplier effect (4 marks):
• More inbound tourists will mean more people would need to be employed in the tourism sector.
• Much needed revenue will be generated to rebuild destroyed infrastructure, particularly in KwaZulu-Natal.
• More employment will mean that more people become tax payers.
• Increased collection of taxes would improve the overall infrastructure.
• Lead to less poverty and criminal activities.
• Will lead to direct and indirect jobs being created.

subQuestions.questionText: Study the World Icons A to F. Identify icons A to F in the pictures. Write only the name of the icon next to the letter. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for each correct icon (max 6 marks):
• A: Mecca / Kaabah
• B: The Parthenon (Athens, Greece)
• C: Mosque / Dome of the Rock
• D: The Blue Mosque (Istanbul, Turkey)
• E: Eiffel Tower (Paris, France)
• F: Taj Mahal

(Accepted icon names include Mecca, Kaabah, Mosque, The Parthenon, Dome of the Rock, The Blue Mosque, Eiffel Tower and Taj Mahal, matched to the correct pictures.)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the difference between an icon and an attraction.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for icon and 2 marks for attraction (max 4 marks):

Icon:
• The country is associated with the icon / it symbolises a country.
• Receives millions of tourists per year.
• High revenue generator.
• Increased publicity for the icon and the country.
• Has unique features.

Attraction:
• Attracts visitors to the area.
• Lesser-known by the rest of the world.
• Attracts fewer tourists.

subQuestions.label: 4.1.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Describe TWO unique features of Icon B. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
B - The Parthenon (Athens, Greece). Award 2 marks for each feature (max 4 marks):
• The Parthenon is the ruins of a temple on top of the Acropolis, a hill in Athens.
• It is a building characterised by pillars (columns).
• Originally built as a temple, it was also used as a treasury, a fortress, a church and a mosque.
• Built in honour of the Greek goddess Athena.

subQuestions.label: 4.1.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Describe TWO unique features of Icon D. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
D - The Blue Mosque (Istanbul, Turkey). Award 2 marks for each feature (max 4 marks):
• It is a mosque with an impressive interior design.
• The roof is unique, with small domes surrounding the bigger dome.
• There are six minarets (small towers) at the Blue Mosque.
• The name comes from the blue ceramic tiles on the inside walls.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss in a paragraph why icon E is considered the most visited icon in France. Your paragraph must include ONE unique feature of this icon and ONE economic benefit for France. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
E - Eiffel Tower (Paris, France). Award 2 marks for unique feature and 2 marks for economic benefit (max 4 marks):

ONE unique feature:
• It is a landmark in the city of Paris.
• It is a symbol of France.
• It is one of the most recognised structures in the world.
• It used to be the tallest structure in the world - 324m high.
• The entire tower is built from iron.
• The whole of Paris can be seen from the top of the tower.

ONE economic benefit for France:
• Higher revenue and foreign currency earnings.
• Contribution to the country's GDP.
• Increased job creation.
• More entrepreneurial opportunities.
• Increased visitor numbers to France.

subQuestions.questionText: Study the information on Mount Fuji. Name the country where Mount Fuji is located.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• Japan

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE negative impact of mass tourism (over-tourism) on Mount Fuji.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE impact:
• Extra strain on the resources in the area, e.g. water, electricity, sanitation.
• Damage to the natural environment.
• Challenges with access control.
• Challenges with management of visitors.
• Increased levels of pollution.

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest TWO sustainable and responsible practices that will result in better management of Mount Fuji.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each practice (max 4 marks):
• Litter bins available along the hiking trails.
• Hiking trails are well demarcated (marked).
• Clear signage of where hikers may go.
• Educational presentations on the natural resources, plants and animals that visitors will see.
• Educational presentations on how to preserve nature and the importance of conservation.
• Encourage climbers to use the routes out of season to reduce the negative impact of too many visitors.
• Charging entrance fees to control crowds.
• Restriction on the number of cars entering the area.
• Regular clean-up of mountain areas.

subQuestions.questionText: Study the pictures of the Gems of the Northern Cape. Identify World Heritage Sites A and B in the pictures. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each site (max 4 marks):
• A: ǂKhomani Cultural Landscape
• B: Richtersveld Cultural and Botanical Landscape

subQuestions.questionText: The San and the Nama people are associated with (linked to) World Heritage Sites A and B. Give ONE reason why it is important to protect the culture of the San and the Nama people.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE reason:
• The culture of the San and Nama should be protected for future generations to experience the traditions and culture of the San and Nama people.
• Protection for future generations.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE way in which the San people showcase their culture to visitors in the area.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE way:
• They take tourists on hunting expeditions and show them how to track the animals.
• The visitors are taken on a tour and are exposed to their simple way of living, their traditions and culture.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss ONE way in which the province benefits from the World Heritage Sites identified in QUESTION 5.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE way:
• Greater publicity for the province.
• Revenue generated can be used to upgrade and maintain the infrastructure.
• Financial benefits for the province, product owners and service providers.
• Decrease in unemployment, poverty and crime.
• Creates jobs and entrepreneurial opportunities which will improve their standard of living.

subQuestions.questionText: Read the information about Africa's Travel Indaba 2022. Give the definition of a travel trade show.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• An event where tourism-related businesses are given the opportunity to exhibit and promote their products and services.
• An event where the major role players in the tourism industry can network in order to establish new business relationships.
• An event where buyers such as tour operators can negotiate business deals with exhibitors.

subQuestions.questionText: SATourism uses Africa's Travel Indaba to market South Africa nationally and internationally. Name ONE other travel trade show held in South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE:
• Getaway Shows (Cape Town and Johannesburg)
• Meetings Africa (Johannesburg / Cape Town)
• Africa's Travel Indaba (KwaZulu-Natal)
• World Travel Market - WTM (Cape Town)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the THREE steps on how the 1% levy collected from tourism businesses is used to market South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each step (max 6 marks):
Step 1: Participating tourism businesses collect the 1% levy from tourists.
Step 2: This money is paid to TOMSA on a monthly basis, who then makes it available to the TBCSA.
Step 3: TBCSA, as administrators of the funds, then pays the money to SATourism.

subQuestions.questionText: Read the 'Room with a better view' Instagram post and the hotel's reaction. Tango Hotels closely monitor their social media platforms and responded within an hour to Mr Mudau's post, moving him to a better room. There are various factors contributing to the professional image of a tourism business. Identify ONE example of professional behaviour by the staff at Tango Hotels.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE example:
• Good communication skills.
• Professional interaction with customers.
• Prompt responses to comments on social media platforms.
NOTE: Accept examples of good communication skills.

subQuestions.questionText: Apart from the image of the staff, identify TWO aspects on the Instagram post that is an indication of the professional image of the hotel.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each aspect (max 4 marks):
• The hotel logo.
• The hotel has a website @TangoHotelsLtd.
• The hotel has social media platforms such as Instagram.
• The hotel monitors their social media platforms closely and responds quickly.
• Customer service policies are implemented.

subQuestions.questionText: Read the information about Royal Tourism Services and their fair labour practices. Explain TWO conditions of employment relating to the remuneration (payment) of staff members.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each condition (max 4 marks):
• The salary is fair payment for the work completed.
• Regular payment of monthly salary/wage.
• The salary is competitive within the sector.
• Amounts deducted from the salary (e.g. UIF) are according to the law.
• Paid for overtime.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the difference between working hours and overtime.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for working hours and 2 marks for overtime (max 4 marks):

Working hours:
• Maximum working hours are specified, e.g. 45 hours per week.
• Normal working hours are part of the contractual obligation.
• Working hours are paid at normal rates.

Overtime:
• Hours worked over and above the required working hours.
• Overtime hours are negotiated to a maximum of 10 hours per week.
• Overtime is paid at a higher rate than ordinary working hours.

subQuestions.questionText: Study the Fair Trade Tourism criteria for tourism businesses. Give TWO examples of how Fair Trade Tourism businesses are involved in social development projects.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each example (max 4 marks):
• Infrastructure
• Education
• Capacity building
• Health
• Sanitation
• Guest contributions

subQuestions.questionText: Apart from the social pillar, identify TWO pillars of sustainable tourism in the Fair Trade Tourism criteria.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each pillar (max 4 marks):
• Economic pillar / profit
• Environmental pillar / planet

subQuestions.questionText: Explain TWO ways in which a certified Fair Trade Tourism business contributes to the local economy.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each way (max 4 marks):
• Local residents are employed by the tourism business.
• The tourism business buys supplies locally or makes use of local services.
• The business procures goods and services from certified Fair Trade Tourism companies.

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons how the phrase, 'Stay where your spend really counts', would encourage responsible tourism practices in South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each reason (max 4 marks):
• It encourages tourists to choose the services of tourism businesses that have been FTT certified.
• It assures tourists that the money that they spend at these establishments will benefit the local community.
• It shows other tourism businesses that tourists prefer to support FTT certified establishments.
• FTT certified companies collaborate to compile and market packages which will appeal to responsible tourists.

subQuestions.questionText: Study the newspaper article about how the war in Ukraine will affect South Africa's tourism industry. Choose the correct word from those given in brackets: Russia and Ukraine are both located in the (Northern/Southern) Hemisphere.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: northern (2 marks)
Russia and Ukraine are both located in the Northern Hemisphere.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify, from the extract, TWO impacts that the war between Russia and the Ukraine has on South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each impact (max 4 marks):
• Higher fuel price / higher petrol price / increase in the price of crude oil.
• Limited supply of wheat / availability of wheat flour / increase in bread prices.

subQuestions.questionText: The impacts identified in QUESTION 9.1.2 will further inconvenience inbound international tourists to South Africa. Discuss THREE ways in which the travel needs of inbound international tourists will be negatively affected during their stay in South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each way (max 6 marks):
• Increased petrol prices will make long distance travel expensive and unaffordable.
• Car hire will be a less popular option because of the cost of petrol.
• The bus/shuttle/taxi industry will suffer - higher ticket prices and availability of fuel.
• Availability, frequency, cancellations and increased cost of flights and other forms of transport will be affected.

subQuestions.questionText: Study the map showing the provincial share of international tourist arrivals in 2020. Arrange the THREE provinces that received the most international visitors to South Africa from the most to the least. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each province in the correct order (max 6 marks). NOTE: Must be in the correct order.
1. Gauteng
2. Western Cape
3. Mpumalanga

subQuestions.questionText: The two least visited provinces were North West (1,1%) and the Northern Cape (0,1%). Give ONE reason for the low international visitor numbers to these provinces.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE reason:
• Long travel distances from the major gateways of the country.
• Limited air access / fewer domestic flights to these provinces.
• These are lesser-known and marketed provinces.
• Limited infrastructure to attract major events.
• Within the province the attractions are situated far apart from each other.

subQuestions.questionText: Study the graph showing the results of the client satisfaction survey for The Blue Fish restaurant. Give ONE reason why the owner of The Blue Fish restaurant felt the need to conduct the survey.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE reason:
• The survey will help identify where and how he can improve his business and increase visitor numbers.
• To get a benchmark for incentives for staff.
• To get a sense of how customers regard his business.

subQuestions.questionText: The owner of The Blue Fish restaurant introduced a cash incentive to his staff as a token of appreciation for good work. Refer to the survey results and identify the staff members who should receive the cash incentives. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• Chef and the team

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons for your answer to QUESTION 10.2. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each reason (max 4 marks):
• The ratings for the chef and the team were the highest.
• The conduct and communication involving frontline staff received low ratings from the customers.
• The cleanliness and maintenance of the restaurant received low ratings.
• The waiters do not take their work seriously.

subQuestions.questionText: Recommend ONE strategy that can be included in the owner's action plan that will result in the increase of visitor numbers and profitability for the restaurant.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE strategy:
• Re-train and up-skill all frontline staff.
• Managers to effectively manage and control staff.
• Make the incentive package attractive to staff.
• Make a supervisor responsible to control the cleanliness and maintenance of the restaurant.
• Do everything in his power to create a memorable experience for guests.
